title: Sign in and choose a workspace
summary: Sign in with Microsoft and open the workspace that matches your approved role.
steps: Open the Service Desk and select Sign in with Microsoft.
After authentication, review the workspaces available to your account: Client portal, Technician workspace, Management workspace, or Administration.
Open only the workspace you are authorized to use.
If a required workspace is missing, ask an administrator to review your role, client/site scope, and permissions.
keywords: login microsoft entra workspace role access
notes: Access is role- and scope-controlled; changing screens does not bypass authorization.

title: Navigate the Service Desk
summary: Use the shared navigation, notification area, workspace switcher, Help, and sign-out controls.
steps: Use the left navigation to open the sections available to your role.
Use Switch workspace to move between Client, Technician, Management, or Administration areas you can access.
Use Notifications in staff workspaces to review ticket-related alerts such as assignment or transfer activity.
Open Help for the User Guide and, for eligible staff, the troubleshooting search tool.
Use Sign out when you finish working on a shared or administrative workstation.
keywords: navigation sidebar workspace switch notifications help sign out
notes: The navigation shown to you changes with your role and permissions.

title: Create a support request
summary: Submit a new support request with the requester, organization, site, category, impact details, and supporting files.
steps: Open My support and choose the new support request area.
Select the requester and the organization; select a site when the issue is location-specific.
Choose the appropriate category.
Enter the subject and describe the problem, impact, when it started, and what has already been tried.
Add relevant screenshots or files when they help explain the issue.
Submit the request and keep the ticket number for follow-up.
keywords: client portal new request ticket organization site category attachment
notes: Client-submitted attachments are requester-visible ticket content.

title: Find and review your support tickets
summary: Search your client-visible tickets and review status, updates, SLA information, conversation, and public attachments.
steps: Open My support tickets.
Use the ticket list to find a request or refresh the current data.
Open a ticket to review its organization, site, status, and current activity.
Review the Conversation section for requester-visible updates and replies.
Check the ticket SLA information shown in the client view when available.
Open any ticket attachment that has been made visible to the client portal.
keywords: client tickets status conversation sla attachments history
notes: Client users see only the ticket information their account is authorized to access.

title: Reply to a client ticket
summary: Add a requester-visible reply to an existing support request and optionally attach supporting files.
steps: Open the ticket from My support tickets.
Review the latest conversation before replying.
Enter your reply in the conversation field.
Add a file when the service desk needs a screenshot, error message, log extract, or other evidence.
Submit the reply and confirm the new message appears in the conversation.
keywords: client reply conversation public attachment screenshot
notes: Client replies are public ticket updates; there is no client-side internal-note control.

title: Use the service catalogue
summary: Start a request from a published service template when the service desk has provided one.
steps: Open Service catalogue.
Search or browse the available published service entries.
Open a service entry and review its description and guidance before starting the request.
Use the request action to start a support ticket from the selected template.
Complete the ticket details and submit the request.
keywords: service catalogue service template request standard service
notes: Published catalogue content can be available to both client users and staff; the request action opens the appropriate ticket workflow for your role.

title: Read published knowledge articles
summary: Search the published knowledge base for guidance that is available to your account.
steps: Open Knowledge base.
Search for a symptom, product, service, or task.
Open an article and review its instructions and visibility.
Follow the documented procedure that applies to your situation.
For staff, use a relevant article to support the ticket resolution and link it to the ticket when appropriate.
keywords: knowledge base article search guidance self service
notes: Only published articles within your authorized visibility are shown.

title: Technician overview and queues
summary: Use the Technician workspace to review queue health, recently updated work, and ticket activity.
steps: Open Technician workspace.
Review the overview metrics and recently updated tickets.
Open Tickets to work from the ticket queue or workflow board.
Use the queue as the working list for tickets within your assigned client/site scope.
Open a ticket to see its complete detail and available controls.
keywords: technician dashboard queue overview workload tickets
notes: Intern, Technician, Team Lead, Manager, and Administrator roles can have staff workspace access, but available actions still depend on permissions and scope.

title: Search tickets and use filters
summary: Find tickets by text, status, priority, client, site, assignee, category, source, tag, SLA state, dates, and location.
steps: Open Tickets in the Technician workspace.
Enter ticket number, subject, requester, client, site, or other supported text in Search tickets.
Add filters such as status, priority, client, site, assigned technician, category, source, tag, or SLA status.
Use Created from and Created to when you need a time range.
Use Location / project when the record contains an office, room, project, or work area.
Run the search and open the ticket that matches the required scope.
keywords: ticket search filter status priority client site assignee category source tag sla date location
notes: Search respects the access scope enforced by the server.

title: Save and reuse ticket views
summary: Save a useful combination of ticket filters as a named view for repeat queue work.
steps: Build the ticket search and filters you use regularly.
Enter a name in the saved-view field.
Save the view.
Select a saved view later to restore the same search criteria.
Delete a saved view when it is no longer useful.
keywords: saved view ticket filter queue reusable search
notes: Saved views belong to the user who created them.

title: Work the team ticket queue
summary: Use the Team Tickets view to work tickets that fall within team-level access.
steps: Open Team Tickets from the staff workspace when it is available to your role.
Review the client/site, status, priority, assignment, and SLA indicators.
Use search and filters to narrow the team queue.
Open a ticket to work it or use the assignment controls provided by your role.
Keep the ticket state and assignment accurate so the queue remains actionable.
keywords: team tickets team queue assignments workload
notes: Team access is controlled by role, permissions, client scope, site scope, and assignment rules.

title: Work internal tickets
summary: Create and work internal-organization tickets that do not belong to a client-facing organization.
steps: Open Internal Tickets when your role is permitted to use internal work.
Review the internal ticket queue and open the required record.
Use the department and internal routing information where provided.
Update the ticket, add internal notes, request specialist help, or assign the work according to your role.
Keep internal ticket content separate from client-facing communication.
keywords: internal ticket department internal work
notes: Internal tickets require a department in the application workflow.

title: Create a technician ticket
summary: Create a ticket manually when a request arrives through a phone call, meeting, Teams reference, or another supported source.
steps: Open New ticket from the Technician workspace.
Select the requester; search by name or email when necessary.
If the requester does not exist, use Add requester and enter the required identity details.
Select the organization and site or location as appropriate.
Enter subject, description, source, source reference, priority, category, and other required ticket information.
Add files when evidence is available and choose the correct attachment visibility.
Submit the ticket and confirm the generated ticket number.
keywords: create ticket manual phone teams requester source priority category
notes: The requester must be associated with the appropriate client scope.

title: Find or add a requester
summary: Use the requester picker when creating a ticket and add a new requester only when the person is not already available.
steps: In the ticket form, start typing the requester name or email.
Select the correct existing requester from the matching results.
When no match exists, choose Add requester.
Enter the requester name and email; provide a phone number when needed.
Save the new requester and continue creating the ticket.
keywords: requester contact add user contact search email phone
notes: Verify the organization/client association before using the requester on the ticket.

title: Review a ticket before taking action
summary: Read the ticket context, history, SLA, assignment, collaboration, approvals, knowledge links, and attachments before changing it.
steps: Open the ticket and confirm the ticket number and subject.
Review requester, client, site, source, location or project, and current assignment.
Read the conversation and activity timeline before replying or changing the ticket.
Check SLA response and resolution targets and note whether the ticket is on track, at risk, breached, paused, or met.
Review linked knowledge, collaboration/help requests, approvals, and attachments.
Decide the next action and record it using the appropriate ticket control.
keywords: ticket detail review context sla history assignment knowledge collaboration approval attachments
notes: Open only tickets within your authorized scope; the API enforces visibility when a ticket is opened.

title: Update ticket status, priority, category and tags
summary: Keep the ticket classification and workflow state accurate as work progresses.
steps: Open the ticket and use Ticket controls.
Update Status when the work moves between the available workflow states.
Set Priority to reflect the urgency defined by your service-desk process.
Set or correct Category so the ticket is reported and measured correctly.
Add or change Tags when the ticket needs operational classification.
Save the change and review the updated SLA and ticket history.
keywords: ticket status priority category tags controls update workflow
notes: Changing priority can recalculate SLA targets according to the configured policy.

title: Claim, assign and transfer tickets
summary: Take ownership of unassigned work or move an assigned ticket to another technician or team.
steps: Open an unassigned ticket and choose Claim ticket when you are allowed to own it.
To assign or transfer, open Assignment and select the target technician allowed by your scope.
Enter a transfer reason when the form requires one.
Save the assignment and review the resulting ticket history or notification.
After a transfer, confirm that the new owner and queue are correct.
keywords: claim assign transfer ownership technician team
notes: Interns cannot assign or transfer tickets in the application.

title: Add public replies and internal notes
summary: Choose public replies for requester-visible communication and internal notes for service-desk-only work.
steps: Open the ticket conversation area.
Choose Public reply when the requester should see the message.
Choose Internal note when the information is for staff only.
Write a clear update that states the action taken, result, next step, or information needed.
Submit the message and review the activity timeline.
For public replies, confirm the reply is queued for requester email when outbound email is enabled.
keywords: public reply internal note comment conversation requester email
notes: Internal notes are not requester-visible and do not send a requester email.

title: Add and manage ticket attachments
summary: Attach evidence to tickets and choose whether each file is staff-only or visible in the client portal.
steps: Open the ticket and use Attachments.
Select a supported file and upload it.
Keep each attachment within the application size limit of 5 MB.
Choose Staff only for internal evidence or Visible in the client portal when the requester should be able to access it.
Confirm the attachment appears in the ticket and review its visibility.
keywords: ticket attachment file upload visibility public internal 5 mb
notes: Do not place passwords, secrets, or unrelated personal data into ticket attachments.

title: Request specialist help and collaborate
summary: Ask a specialist or department to assist with a ticket and track the collaboration request.
steps: Open Collaboration & help on the ticket.
Choose either a specialist person or a department.
Describe the exact expertise, review, or action you need.
Submit the help request and wait for the response.
When the request is accepted, review the resulting collaborator or response information.
Continue to document the technical work in the ticket timeline.
keywords: collaboration specialist help request department expert assistance
notes: Specialist-help routing uses internal department membership and expertise information.

title: Request and record ticket approvals
summary: Use the ticket approval control when a management decision is required.
steps: Open the ticket and review the work and evidence before requesting approval.
Choose Request approval and enter a clear reason for the decision needed.
Submit the request and confirm the ticket shows a pending approval state.
An authorized approver opens the approval control, reviews the request, and records the decision and decision note.
After the decision, review the ticket history and approval state before continuing work.
keywords: ticket approval request approve reject decision management
notes: Interns cannot request ticket approval; approval decisions require the configured ticket approval permission.

title: Review ticket notifications
summary: Use the notification center to review assignment and ticket-work alerts.
steps: Open the notification center from a staff workspace header.
Review unread ticket notifications such as assignments and transfers.
Open the related ticket from the notification when you need to take action.
Return to the ticket queue after handling the notification.
keywords: notifications alerts assignment transfer ticket
notes: Notification availability depends on the user role and the event generated by the ticket workflow.

title: Search and manage knowledge from a ticket
summary: Use the Knowledge base to find relevant published or staff-visible procedures and link useful articles to tickets.
steps: Open Knowledge base and search by symptom, product, service, or task.
Review the article content and visibility before using it.
When the article is relevant to the ticket, open the ticket and use Find and link an article.
Select the relevant article and verify it appears under Linked knowledge.
Use the linked article to support a repeatable resolution or client explanation.
keywords: knowledge article link ticket published staff client procedure
notes: Knowledge articles can have category, visibility, publication status, and ticket-link relationships.

title: Use approved web troubleshooting help
summary: Search general troubleshooting sources from the Help bubble without sending client-specific or sensitive information to the search service.
steps: Open the Help bubble in a technician, team-lead, manager, or administrator workspace.
Describe the general symptom and environment without using client names, ticket numbers, hostnames, IP addresses, URLs, credentials, or personal data.
Run Find troubleshooting steps.
Review the returned sources and extracted procedures before acting.
Verify the procedure against your approved internal guidance and record relevant findings in the ticket.
keywords: help web search troubleshooting approved sources brave searxng
notes: Web guidance requires configuration and is limited to general troubleshooting prompts. The application rejects prompts containing ticket numbers, addresses, IPs, URLs, credentials, or personal data.

title: Review incoming email intake
summary: Use Email administration to inspect messages that need review before they are linked to tickets or turned into new tickets.
steps: Open Email administration and review the Delivery and reply processing table.
Look for messages in REVIEW, FAILED, or UNKNOWN states.
Open Review for the message that needs attention.
Read the sender, subject, body, state, and available attachment information.
Choose the appropriate review action: ignore the message or attach it to an existing ticket/change when supported.
Enter a review reason and record the decision.
keywords: email intake review incoming message review queue unknown failed ticket
notes: Ambiguous inbound mail is intentionally routed to review rather than being attached to the wrong record.

title: Create a ticket from an inbound email
summary: Create a ticket from an inbound message when automatic matching did not create one.
steps: Open an inbound ticket-channel message that is in REVIEW.
Choose Create a ticket from this email.
Select the organization that owns the message.
Select the saved requester whose email matches the sender.
Select the site when the message is location-specific.
Select the ticket category.
Create the ticket and confirm the email is associated with it.
keywords: email create ticket manual intake requester client site category
notes: The intake form asks you to match the sender to a saved contact before creating the ticket.

title: Review email delivery and reply history
summary: Use email delivery records and ticket mail timelines to understand inbound and outbound processing.
steps: Open Email administration to see mailbox synchronization timestamps and message states.
Use Review for messages in REVIEW, FAILED, or UNKNOWN states.
Open a ticket or change email timeline when you need the message history associated with that record.
Review the message direction, channel, subject, state, and error code before retrying or relinking it.
For uncertain outbound delivery, confirm the SMTP provider result before retrying.
keywords: email delivery reply processing timeline smtp retry failed unknown
notes: Retrying an uncertain outbound message can create a duplicate if the provider already delivered it.

title: Configure email connections and routing
summary: Configure outbound SMTP, incoming Microsoft 365/Graph intake, the ticket mailbox, and client recipient routing.
steps: Open Email administration.
Configure the SMTP server, port, encryption mode, username, and password as approved for your environment.
Set the ticket mailbox used for service-desk email.
Choose Disabled or Microsoft 365 / Graph for the incoming mailbox connection.
Enable outgoing email only after the SMTP settings are verified.
Use Verify SMTP connection to test the connection.
Use Send ticket test to me when outbound email is enabled and confirm delivery.
Configure recipient-to-client routes and test each route before broad intake is enabled.
keywords: email administration smtp2go smtp microsoft 365 graph mailbox routing
notes: CAB email is disabled in the current application flow; change communication is recorded in the change workspace instead.

title: Management overview and workload
summary: Use the Management workspace to monitor ticket workload, SLA status, and approvals across the scope available to management.
steps: Open Management workspace.
Review the dashboard workload and recent activity.
Use Tickets to inspect the broader ticket queue.
Review SLA information and approvals when prioritizing or escalating work.
Open a ticket when a management decision or intervention is required.
keywords: management dashboard workload tickets sla approvals
notes: Management access is available to Team Leads, Managers, and Administrators.

title: Monitor and manage the management ticket queue
summary: Use Management Tickets for wider queue oversight, filtering, and ticket-level intervention.
steps: Open Management → Tickets.
Search and filter the ticket list using the available criteria.
Review assignment, priority, SLA, and current status.
Open a ticket when reassignment, approval, escalation, or another management action is required.
Record decisions in the ticket using the appropriate public, internal, assignment, or approval control.
keywords: management tickets oversight queue escalation assignment approval
notes: Management views can expose a wider scope than an individual technician queue.

title: Review and maintain SLA policies
summary: Use SLA Management to maintain response and resolution policies, calendars, and warning behavior.
steps: Open SLA Management.
Review the active SLA policies and the priority each policy applies to.
Set response and resolution targets in minutes.
Set the warning percentage used to flag approaching targets.
Review the working calendar associated with each policy.
Use the calendar editor to maintain timezone, working days, start/end times, and holiday entries.
Save the policy or calendar and verify a sample ticket receives the expected SLA target.
keywords: sla management response resolution warning calendar working days holidays
notes: The same SLA configuration is used by ticket-level SLA calculations.

title: Use reports and analytics
summary: Review ticket, SLA, technician, and service metrics using the reporting views available to your role.
steps: Open Reports & Analytics or Service performance.
Select the required client, technician, date range, or other report filters available on the screen.
Review the resulting metrics and ticket lists.
Use the Service performance view when you need a focused performance summary.
Use the technician export controls when you need CSV or Excel output from the technician reporting view.
keywords: reports analytics technician report export csv excel service performance metrics
notes: Report access is permission-controlled; an administrator can also expose service performance through the shared navigation.

title: Use the change register and calendar
summary: Review planned changes, risk, status, owner, and planned windows before scheduling or approving work.
steps: Open Change Management.
Review the Change register table for change number, type, risk, status, owner, and planned window.
Open a change to review its full record.
Use the Change calendar to inspect planned windows and potential scheduling conflicts.
Create a new change when controlled work must be recorded.
keywords: change register calendar risk status owner planned window
notes: Change access is separately controlled and can be Contributor, Coordinator, Approver, or Change Manager.

title: Create a controlled service change
summary: Create a change with its scope, risk, impact, implementation, test, rollback, communication, and stakeholder information.
steps: Open Change Management and select New change.
Start from a saved change template when a standard plan already exists, or choose Blank change.
Select the organization, site, lead department, and owner.
Enter the change title, description, category, change type, and risk.
Record expected downtime and whether an outage is expected.
Set whether the client should be notified where approved.
Set the planned start and end.
Complete impact assessment, reason, business justification, implementation plan, test/validation plan, rollback plan, and communication plan.
Add client-side contacts or external stakeholders as required.
Attach change evidence when you have supporting files, then submit the change.
keywords: new change change template risk impact implementation test rollback stakeholders downtime
notes: The change form supports up to 10 attachments, with a maximum of 5 MB per file in the current UI.

title: Review a change and its control plan
summary: Use the change detail page to review assessment, scheduling, linked incidents, approvals, teams, stakeholders, evidence, updates, communications, and immutable history.
steps: Open the change from the register or a linked record.
Review the planned window, risk, assessment, and control information.
Check the CAB, scheduling and review panel for readiness and schedule conflicts.
Review linked incident tickets and confirm they belong to the same organization where required.
Review approval requests, implementation teams, stakeholders, attachments, updates, communications, and history.
Use the available actions only when your change-access role permits them.
keywords: change detail control plan linked incidents approvals teams stakeholders evidence updates history
notes: Changing controlled fields can create a new revision and clear approval readiness; previous decisions remain in history.

title: Manage change approvals
summary: Record individual or CAB approval decisions and track readiness for the current change revision.
steps: Open the change and review the current revision and approval readiness.
Review existing approval requests and the required decision path.
When authorized, add an individual or department approver.
Record APPROVED, REJECTED, or CHANGES_REQUESTED with a decision note.
Review the number of independent and CAB approvals and the readiness messages.
Do not assume approval is complete until the current revision meets the configured requirements.
keywords: change approval cab independent approvals decisions readiness revision
notes: Approver, Coordinator, Change Manager, and Administrator access is controlled separately from general staff access.

title: Manage change teams, tasks and updates
summary: Assign implementation teams, add tasks, record progress, and document validation or communication updates.
steps: Open the Implementation teams and tasks section of the change.
Add the responsible department/team and the appropriate role such as Implementer, Lead, or Reviewer.
Add implementation tasks with a title, instructions, department, and assignee.
Update task state as TODO, IN_PROGRESS, BLOCKED, COMPLETED, or WAIVED.
Record a progress update when task status changes or evidence is available.
Use Team updates to record internal, implementation, validation, or client-communication notes.
keywords: change implementation team task todo progress blocked completed validation updates
notes: Keep implementation evidence and validation notes inside the change record so reviewers can reconstruct what occurred.

title: Manage change stakeholders, evidence and history
summary: Maintain external stakeholders, change evidence, update history, communications, and immutable change history.
steps: Open the Stakeholders section and review existing contacts.
Add a client contact or an external stakeholder with name, email, and stakeholder role when required.
Use Attachments and evidence to upload supporting files.
Use Team updates to document implementation or validation evidence.
Review Communication history for recorded communication events.
Use Immutable change history to trace significant events and decisions.
keywords: change stakeholders attachments evidence communication history audit immutable
notes: The current change workflow records communications and decisions; CAB email delivery is disabled.

title: Configure CAB and change policy
summary: Administrators can maintain CAB groups, quorum, templates, blackout windows, and post-implementation review requirements.
steps: Open CAB & change policy from Administration or the staff navigation.
Review the policy flags for CAB requirements, independent approvals, and post-implementation review.
Create or edit CAB groups and set the quorum and reviewers.
Create or update change templates for recurring plans.
Create blackout windows for organizations, sites, or periods where changes should be restricted.
Review post-implementation requirements and record follow-up when a change closes.
keywords: cab change policy quorum reviewers templates blackout post implementation review governance
notes: Changing governance affects future and in-progress change workflows; make changes deliberately and verify a sample change afterward.

title: Use the Administration overview
summary: Review service-desk administration counts, recent activity, and links to configuration areas.
steps: Open Administration.
Review the overview counts for users, tickets, clients, sites, and assets.
Use the navigation to open the configuration section you need.
Review Audit History when you need to verify administrative changes.
Use the dashboard links to move directly to the corresponding configuration records.
keywords: admin overview counts configuration users clients sites assets dashboard
notes: Administrative sections can be permission-restricted even for non-Administrator staff with delegated management permissions.

title: Manage users and access
summary: Provision and maintain Service Desk access using verified Microsoft Entra identities, roles, scope, departments, and change access.
steps: Open Users & Access.
When adding a user, search Azure using the name, work email, or Entra UPN.
Select the exact verified Entra account.
Choose one access profile: Client user, Intern, Technician, Team Lead, Manager, or Administrator.
For staff roles, set work scope, Change Management access, supervisor where applicable, departments, expertise, client scope, and optional site scope.
For client users, make sure the correct client membership is selected.
Save the access profile and confirm the user appears with the intended active state.
keywords: users access entra azure role technician team lead manager admin intern work scope client scope site departments
notes: Changing an existing user profile signs the user out of existing sessions. At least one active administrator must remain.

title: Grant or remove client portal access
summary: Link an approved client contact to a user account so that the person can access the client portal.
steps: Open Contacts and select the client contact.
Use the portal-access control on the contact record.
Choose the approved portal account or select No portal access.
Save the portal link.
Ask the user to sign in again and verify that the Client portal workspace is available.
keywords: contact portal account client user link access
notes: The client user role and contact-to-account linkage work together to provide client portal access.

title: Manage clients
summary: Create and maintain organizations, ticket number prefixes, contact information, and client notes.
steps: Open Clients.
Add or edit the client name, ticket prefix, primary email, primary phone, and notes.
Use an uppercase ticket prefix that matches the allowed format.
Save the client and review its active/inactive state.
Use the client record when managing related contacts, sites, assets, and user memberships.
keywords: clients organizations ticket prefix primary email phone notes
notes: Changing a client ticket prefix affects only future tickets.

title: Manage contacts
summary: Maintain client contacts and associate them with the correct organization and optional site.
steps: Open Contacts.
Create or edit the contact name, email, and phone.
Select the client organization.
Select a site when the contact is site-specific; leave it blank for an organization-wide contact.
Save the contact and use the portal-access control when this contact should be linked to a client user.
keywords: contacts client requester site email phone portal
notes: Contacts referenced by retained ticket history may be deactivated instead of permanently deleted.

title: Manage sites and assets
summary: Maintain client sites and tracked assets used for ticket routing and operational context.
steps: Open Sites and select the client organization.
Create or update the site name and address.
Open the relevant client context when adding an asset.
Enter asset name, asset type, serial number, external reference, and site when applicable.
Save the records and verify their client/site association.
keywords: sites address assets serial number asset type external reference client
notes: Assets are client-scoped and can also be associated with a site.

title: Manage ticket categories
summary: Maintain ticket categories, descriptions, and optional parent/child relationships used for classification and SLA policy application.
steps: Open Categories.
Add a category name and description.
Select a parent category when creating a child category.
Save the category and verify the hierarchy.
Review a sample ticket to confirm the category is available and applies as expected.
keywords: categories parent child hierarchy ticket classification
notes: Category changes affect how new and updated tickets are classified and reported.

title: Manage ticket tags
summary: Create and maintain reusable tags for ticket classification, searching, and operational filtering.
steps: Open Tags.
Create a tag name and optional description.
Edit the tag when its meaning or description changes.
Use the tag on tickets where it improves filtering or reporting.
Review ticket search filters to confirm the tag is available.
keywords: tags classification filter ticket search reporting
notes: Keep tag names consistent so technicians can find and reuse the same classifications.

title: Review tickets from Administration
summary: Use the administrative ticket view to inspect tickets when broader administrative scope is required.
steps: Open Administration → Tickets.
Search and filter the ticket data using the administrative view.
Open a ticket to review the same ticket history, SLA, assignments, approvals, attachments, and controls available to your administrative role.
Use the administrative view for investigation or oversight rather than bypassing normal ticket workflow.
keywords: admin tickets administration ticket detail oversight
notes: Administrative visibility does not remove the need to use the correct ticket action or audit trail.

title: Use Reports & Analytics administration view
summary: Review operational reporting from the Administration workspace and use the available filters and exports.
steps: Open Reports & Analytics.
Set the date range and any available client, technician, priority, or calendar filters.
Review policy and workload information shown on the page.
Use the technician export links when you need CSV or Excel output.
Open a related ticket from the report when further investigation is needed.
keywords: admin reports analytics technician export csv excel metrics filters
notes: Exported reports should be handled according to your organization’s data-handling rules.

title: Review service performance
summary: Use the Service performance view for a focused operational report across the ticket and SLA data you are allowed to see.
steps: Open Service performance from the shared navigation when it is available to your role.
Set the reporting period and available scope filters.
Review the resulting performance information.
Use the results to identify tickets that need follow-up, escalation, or deeper review.
keywords: service performance report reporting period scope ticket sla
notes: The Service performance link is shown to administrators and users with the reports permission.

title: Review audit history
summary: Trace important administrative and ticket-related changes using the recorded audit history.
steps: Open Audit History.
Search or filter the available audit records.
Review the actor, action, entity, timestamp, and recorded details.
Open the related record when further context is needed.
Use the audit trail to support investigations and change reviews.
keywords: audit history logs actor action entity timestamp investigation
notes: Audit records are historical evidence; do not edit or delete them as part of normal troubleshooting.

title: Use the complete User Guide
summary: Search this guide by section, feature, or task and open the relevant workspace page from each topic.
steps: Open User guide from the shared navigation.
Use the search box with a feature name such as ticket, SLA, attachment, email, change, or user.
Read the Steps and Important notes for the matching topic.
Select Open this section → to go directly to the related workspace page.
Return to the guide when you need instructions for another role or function.
keywords: user guide help documentation search topic instructions
notes: The guide is role-filtered, so users may see different topics based on their authorized access.
